verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes' 57 source-warrant occurrences (~50 unique URLs) by retrieval against doc.rust-lang.org, docs.rs, github.com, v8.dev, nodejs.org, webassembly.github.io, blog.rust-lang.org and nnethercote's perf-book; checked all six engine_note claims against the live si-rpg-engine repo via gh api (solver/Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/rapier_law.rs, build.mjs, FLAGS.md, Cargo.lock); and ran the lane's full compile_oracle.py suite plus 20+ of my own counter-examples directly against rustc 1.98.1, including the obscure ones (E0518's retirement text, E0463 on wasm32 -Cprofile-generate, E0587/E0589, the IEEE kernel's exact hex bits reproduced on host and wasm32, and this host's own 'arrowlake-s' target-cpu=native feature counts, which matched the recipe's claimed 38-vs-5 numbers exactly). Mid-task, a relayed message claimed the input had been regenerated with additional no_warnings/wasm_no_imports check fields; I independently diffed the live file rather than trust the claim, and found only three added no_warnings:true fields (recipe 1 check 2, recipe 4 check 3, recipe 9 check 5) with no wasm_no_imports anywhere in this lane — my full-lane oracle run had already been executed against that current file and passed all three cleanly. Every source resolved and supported its claim; every engine fact matched the live repository verbatim; all 41 oracle checks passed; nothing was found stale, mismatched, fabricated or unfindable. The systemic weakness is structural, not factual: as a performance lane, its central practical numbers (V8 timings, byte-size deltas, wasm sample-percentage splits) are single-machine, single-scene, unreproducible-by-a-verifier measurements -- properly scoped throughout (rep counts, sampling intervals, and noise bounds are stated) but resting on trust in the research agent's own measurement process, since no citation or compiler check can confirm a wall-clock number. Recipe 8 (profile-the-law-natively) is the sharpest instance: it carries zero compiler checks, so every one of its claims is anchored by documentation and engine facts alone, never by executable proof.
